look_here_first: TEXAS FESCUE / FESTUCA VERSUTA — a native woodland or wooded limestone grass with a persistent PERENNIAL bunch base, long delicate leafy shoots and a usually looser branching panicle of separate multi-flowered spikelets. The new 1906 public-domain 'Festuca johnsoni Vasey' plate (an older taxonomic concept later synonymized with F. versuta) sketches a tuft, open panicle and enlarged reproductive parts; it is NOT a modern, taxon-reconfirmed photograph. Our only physically archived F. versuta JPG still shows loose grass fragments, not a live crown. Keep species ID PROVISIONAL until a verified flowering specimen and whole plant are photographed.

best_field_traits: North American native perennial; exact Hays County occurrence remains unreviewed.
Grass identification should be based on intact plant and spikelets, not scattered seed material.
Perennial crown and taller flowering culms versus small sixweeks annual.
Open to somewhat nodding panicle with multi-flowered fescue spikelets (must verify with intact source-identified individual).
Leaf sheath ligule and any awns require scale macro; current photo insufficient.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Entire identified Texas fescue plant and rooted perennial base
Whole mature panicle showing branches and intact spikelets
True ligule, leaf blade cross section with millimeter scale
Glumes/lemmas and awns on intact mature spikelet verified by expert key
crew_field_check: Start from whole rooted plant to establish growth form.
Photograph flowering head and collar on same individual.
Use hand-lens/25x macro to measure floret structure when needed; photos without it support only provisional source determination.
Taxon synonym Vulpia octoflora is the same installed Festuca octoflora concept, not a new species admission. Texas fescue specific county occurrence not audited.

comparisons.key_distinctions: F. octoflora / Vulpia octoflora is a small short-lived annual with very thin leaves and narrow awned upright panicle. F. versuta is a perennial and may show a more branching panicle and an enduring crown; verify this in a fresh whole-plant image because current loose-bract photo cannot separate them reliably. Also compare Festuca subverticillata/nutans concepts with a regional taxonomic key.

items.label: TEXAS FESCUE — HISTORIC 1906 Festuca johnsoni anatomical plate
items.image_role: HISTORIC BOTANICAL ILLUSTRATION, NOT A PHOTOGRAPH. The 1906 Smithsonian / U.S. National Herbarium plate says 'Festuca johnsoni Vasey', corresponding to Festuca nutans var. johnsonii Vasey / F. johnsonii (Vasey) Piper synonym complex under accepted F. versuta. Contains a rooted/tillered plant, a loose panicle on branch tips, exaggerated detached spikelet, and enlarged bract drawings.
items.caption: Old plate illustrates a thin flowering culm rising from a tufted base, long narrow foliage, an airy branching panicle and separate enlarged spikelet/blade-anatomy drawings. Useful for HOW to recognize reproductive organization but not an exact measured present-day Texas fescue voucher, a live color photo, or proof of all microstructures.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a real historical taxonomic illustration of a synonymous name where the one current Texas-fescue source image shows only loose fragments. Shows field architecture without manufacturing a plant photograph.
